Adding network specifics and what I'll run during the pre-cut and cutover window. I attached a short snippet file with the exact commands I plan to execute for prefix checks and interface health.

Pre-cut network checks (Connor owner):
- Verify BGP UP for transit peer(s): show ip bgp summary | match <acme-prefixes>
- Confirm route propagation into infra routing tables (expected prefixes: 10.200.0.0/16, 10.201.0.0/16)
- Validate ACLs and NAT rules (tcp 443/80) and ensure stateful inspection is passing
- Run packet capture for TLS handshake validation (10s) and confirm SAN matches the cert on the private endpoint

Cutover steps I will execute:
- Shift a small mirror of production-like traffic to private endpoint (10% of synthetic load)
- Observe ECMP path distribution and re-run traceroutes to confirm symmetry
- On detection of any blackholing or asymmetric NAT, revert route advertisement immediately (I will coordinate via ops bridge)

If anything fails: immediate rollback to prior route advertisement and notify on bridge; I will pair with Marissa to validate telemetry and with Hiro for runtime issues.

Couple runtime items to call out for the runbook (I'll own runtime warmup):
- KV cache priming: I will run kv_warmup.sh against the private endpoint before full traffic cutover; script ramps keys over 15 minutes to reach steady-state memory occupancy.
- Model warmup: run scripted prompts at 5 rps across the primary model variants to pre-populate attention caches; results logged to /var/log/redwood/warmup.log
- Health endpoints: /health and /v1/status must return 200 and the KV cache size metric > threshold
- Temp memory and GPU temp checks: if GPU mem exceeds 90% on any node during warmup we will pause and scale out a notch (autoscale preconfigured for reserved pool)

I'll attach the warmup script for review. Plan: start warmup 20m before the synthetic traffic scale step so cache and kernels are hot.
